newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN suspended, 149.1 Fr requote cap.
newsitem.headline: GAN suspended, 149.1 Fr requote cap.

text.p: Share trading in state-controlled insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales were suspended four times in a row on the Paris bourse on Friday and would requote only if they stayed under a ceiling of 149.10 francs, the SBF stock markets association said.

The shares were suspended at 123 francs on Thursday ahead of a government announcement of a state rescue package costing up to 20 billion francs to shore up the company's accounts after 35 billion francs of losses since 1992.
Several attempts to requote were abandoned after the share price repeatedly breached limits triggering a halt in trading.

"Obviously the market's assumption is that the government is pretty much writing out a blank cheque and not diluting shareholders," one insurance analyst said in reaction to the price move and rescue package.
"It's really a transfer of value to the part of minority interests," the analyst said.
Also underpinning the rise, he said, "is the assumption that a clean GAN, shorn of its defeasance and property troubles, would be a much more palatable bid target."

Speculation has been renewed in the stock market recently that consolidation in the sector could mean more mergers, with some traders suggesting the possibility of a bid for GAN by rival private French insurer AGF.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday that the government would inject 11 billion francs into GAN this year, seven billion to cover losses at the UIC property unit which has run up losses of 30 billion francs in three years, and 3.9 billion francs for GAN Assurances.
The state could pay out another nine billion francs to cover losses on property loans and sales, Arthuis said.

He said he wanted to insulate the profitable banking unit CIC and the insurance division from a "diseased" UIC and property defeasance business, and privatise CIC and GAN Assurances "during the course of 1997".
